I am a 33-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I finished middle school and then came back to work the land with my father. I have about 8 mu of family land, and like most households here, I follow the wheat–maize double-cropping system. That is what our soil, climate, and water timing suit best, and it is what the buyers and machinery services are set up for.

My winter wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October, right after the National Day holiday. I used Luyuan 502, an improved variety that my neighbors have had good luck with. Right now it is greening up after winter dormancy, so my immediate work is the spring topdressing and first irrigation. I will spread urea when the wheat reaches the reviving-green stage, and irrigate twice more before harvest around early June — once at jointing and once at filling. I do rotary tillage before wheat sowing every autumn to break up the soil and bury the maize stubble. I apply compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then straight nitrogen as topdressing. I also spray herbicide once in spring, and I usually need one or two insecticide/fungicide applications because powdery mildew and aphids show up every year. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu this year if the weather cooperates.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. I never till for maize — I just drill the seeds directly into the wheat stubble. Everyone here uses Denghai 605, a hybrid seed that gives high yield if you water it. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then side-dress urea at the jointing stage. Maize only needs about two irrigations in summer: one at the big喇叭口 stage and one at flowering, because the summer rains usually help. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide once or twice for corn borer. I expect roughly 1,150 jin per mu from the maize.

I do not grow cotton. My cousin tried it a few years ago, and while the price per jin is higher, cotton needs too much hand labor and too many pesticide sprays. With only my wife and parents to help, I cannot manage the picking and pruning. Wheat and maize let me use the combine harvester and seed drill, and I can sell both grains at the collection point in town the same day. This year, I will stick to what I know.
